# Antagonist Standard Operating Procedure
Your role type decides which rules bind you for the round. You hold a role type [bold]only[/bold] if the game explicitly tells you so - never by inference, never because of what you are carrying, and never because another player says so.
## Crew Aligned / Non-Antagonist
The default. If the game has not told you otherwise, this is you.
Crew-aligned players are expected to work toward a net positive effect on the round. Most players are this most rounds.
## Solo Antagonist
Roles intended to cause problems for the round or for the crew. You are a solo antagonist only where the game clearly and explicitly says so.
Antagonists are exempt from many roleplay rules, [bold]but not all of them[/bold], and never from the core rules.
## Team Antagonist
As a solo antagonist, but with teammates. You are expected [bold]not[/bold] to hinder them, and may be expected to help them.
## Free Agent
Free to act as an antagonist or as crew, and free to change your mind at any point in the round.
## Familiar
A non-antagonist bound to obey one specific person - the one the game names, and no other.
That obedience holds [bold]even where it breaks roleplay rules or gets you killed[/bold].
## Silicon / Altered Silicon
Bound by their lawset above all else except the core rules.
[bold]Altered Silicon[/bold] is functionally identical; the label marks a lawset that has been hacked, corrupted, or is otherwise non-standard or dangerous.
## Further Reading
[italic]For the rules governing antagonist conduct, see [textlink="Section 11. Antagonists" link="RuleC11"].[/italic]
